actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository releases a benchmark whose eval/ directory is a self-contained MuJoCo sim2sim harness built on numpy, mujoco and torch
The robot/g1_29dof/ directory is the exact Unitree G1 29-DoF MuJoCo plant the policy was validated on
The physical-robot runtime is the Holosoma two-process stack, and that framework and the Unitree SDK are not bundled in this repository
The rollout module imports mujoco directly and is a self-contained MuJoCo rollout
The default robot XML is robot/g1_29dof/g1_29dof.xml
The model file is the MJCF document named g1_29dof, compiled in radians with its meshes under ./meshes/
The deploy loader drops the contact pair block, injects a floor plane and rewrites the mesh directory before compiling the model
The physics timestep is SIM_DT = 0.0005 s (2000 Hz)
G1Sim assigns model.opt.timestep = SIM_DT after loading the deploy model
The plant has one free base joint and the 29 policy joints, and G1Sim skips the first 7 qpos and 6 qvel entries of the free joint
G1Sim.step advances the physics with mujoco.mj_step(self.model, self.data)
The pelvis body carries the freejoint named floating_base_joint inside the body with childclass g1_29dof

The 29 motor actuators are named after the 29 joints; hip pitch/roll/yaw and waist yaw use +-88, knee +-139, ankle pitch/roll and waist roll/pitch +-50, shoulder, elbow and wrist roll +-25, and wrist pitch/yaw +-5, all as actuator ctrlrange
The model declares a contact block of 14 foot<->floor pairs whose second geom is named floor
The sensor block declares pelvis frame quaternion, gyro and accelerometer sensors, and mid360 frame quaternion and position sensors
The bundled G1 model and meshes derive from Unitree's BSD-3-Clause model; the notice attributes the actuator and visual-group modifications to Apache-2.0 Holosoma

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the model XML for the qpos/qvel dimensions, the 29 actuator control ranges and the option timestep, but integrates a placeholder effort-driven acceleration using unit inverse inertia, rather than a position servo

no mesh, texture, inertia, contact, friction, tendon, equality or actuator constraint is resolved; the foot<->floor contact pairs the upstream drops are not modelled and the free base is not integrated
the stand-in reports the initial free-base position and identity orientation and never moves the base, so balance and contact trajectories are not the engine's

the snapshot uses the bridge's basic profile (time and actuator activation) because the stand-in does not provide mj_getState, mj_setState, mj_stateSize or mjtState; the real engine offers the full integration-state profile
MuJoCo was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine, and the real sim backend was not run

the raw model file sets no timestep and references an undefined floor geom; the driver applies the upstream deploy-scene patch at load time (drop the contact block, inject the floor plane, absolute meshdir) and writes the upstream SIM_DT of 0.0005 s, but that patched scene was not compiled here
the package serves the model's raw torque channels; the upstream G1Sim's PD controller, its 29-joint q_target interface, its observation builder and the DDC policy are not part of this driver
no physical Unitree G1 is modelled or controlled and nothing was validated against hardware: the repository's on-robot runtime and Unitree SDK are not bundled (DEPLOYMENT.md:7-10)
rendering and the sensor block are not exposed; the package serves only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: this endpoint's lockstep world stops advancing: no step or world reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; qpos, qvel and ctrl are retained and readable, and clearing the latch alone integrates no physics
